\section{Exact normalized-kernel interface for Yang--Mills}

For a retained boundary state \(s\), compact conditional fiber \(F_s\),
positive fiber weight \(w_s(f)\), next-state map \(\tau(s,f)\), and bad region
\(B_s\), define
\begin{align}
 Z(s)&=\int_{F_s}w_s(f)\,df,\\
 Q(s,A)&=\frac1{Z(s)}
 \int_{B_s}\mathbf 1_{\{\tau(s,f)\in A\}}w_s(f)\,df.
\end{align}
For any positive \(V\), the exact weighted bad row is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:physical-row}
 q_V(s)=\frac{1}{Z(s)V(s)}
 \int_{B_s}w_s(f)V(\tau(s,f))\,df.
\end{equation}
No action-only estimate can replace the normalizer \(Z(s)\).

H1 proposes to obtain or approximate \(V\) from a positive principal
eigenfunction.  There are two admissible routes.

\paragraph{Temporal-vacuum route.}
Construct a reflection-positive temporal transfer operator
\(T_{a,L}\), prove a strictly positive vacuum eigenfunction \(\psi_{a,L}\),
and show that the retained-state conditional kernel is its Doob transform or
a controlled approximation.  Then use \(V_{a,L}=\psi_{a,L}^{-1}\).

\paragraph{Exploration-Perron route.}
Construct the complete normalized bad subkernel \(Q_{a,L}\) directly and find
a positive Lyapunov eigenweight.  This can prove defect suppression, but the
eigenweight is not called a physical vacuum without a temporal-transfer
identification.

Both routes must prove, uniformly over finite volume, cutoff, and every
positive-mass retained history,
\begin{align}
 Q_{a,L}V_{a,L}&\le qV_{a,L},\qquad q<\crit,\\
 \nu_{a,L}(V_{a,L})&\le M<\infty.
\end{align}
The state must retain continuous collar, center, cut/orbit, and
compositionally sufficient integer topology data.  Gauge covariance,
reflection compatibility, chart complements, partition normalizers, and
cross-channel persistence remain explicit proof obligations.

The first open implication is therefore not Perron theory.  It is the
construction and uniform analytic control of the physical nonlinear kernel
appearing in~\eqref{eq:physical-row}.
